entries.prompt: Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. White background, navy headings and outlines, muted teal/blue emphasis, orange for risk. Flat illustrated textbook style, crisp large sans-serif lettering, generous whitespace, few words. Diagram relationships and pictorial meaning are more important than decoration. All requested labels must be exact, readable, and correctly spelt in British English. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'TECHNICAL POWER BRINGS RESPONSIBILITY'. A large left-to-right three-stage illustrated chain. LEFT: a programmer at a laptop with a document bearing a warning icon; label 'Specialist knowledge', below it 'A hidden safety fault'. CENTRE: a clearly separated decision/document panel with an honest report, label 'Professional duty', below it 'Disclose and explain the risk'. RIGHT: a customer studying the report, with a small bridge and people nearby, label 'Informed decision', below it 'Protect people who depend on the system'. Draw just two arrows: specialist knowledge -> professional duty -> informed decision. Below these, a simple support strip with a book icon, connected peers icon and learning icon labelled respectively 'Code of conduct', 'Peer guidance', 'Continuing development'; bracket them under 'Professional-body support'. Footer: 'Support does not replace personal responsibility.' The professional body supports judgement; do not show it automatically certifying a product, guaranteeing safety, or replacing testing.

SECOND: inside the central safety report remove the signature, 'Signed:', 'Date:' and the invented date '22 May 2025'. Show an illustrated route map with a wheelchair symbol facing stairs, labelled 'Route incorrectly marked accessible'. From this shared situation draw two separate downward branches with arrowheads. LEFT teal branch: developer reporting a warning labelled 'Report and correct' -> corrected route map labelled 'Users can avoid the unsuitable route'. Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. White background, navy headings and outlines, muted teal/blue emphasis, orange for risk. Flat illustrated textbook style, crisp large sans-serif lettering, generous whitespace, few words. Diagram relationships and pictorial meaning are more important than decoration. All requested labels must be exact, readable, and correctly spelt in British English. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'COPYRIGHT AND LICENCE PERMISSIONS'. Draw a copyright holder represented by a person beside an original source-code document bearing a plain copyright symbol. An arrow labelled 'Grants permission through a licence' leads to a large licence document centrally. From the licence draw three distinct branches to illustrated activities: a computer labelled 'Run'; a code editor with pencil labelled 'Modify'; two partner offices exchanging copies labelled 'Redistribute'. Each activity has its own small label 'If permitted'. Beneath, a small visual of a copyright notice still attached to a redistributed copy, caption 'Conditions can continue to apply'. Footer exact: 'Publishing source does not itself remove copyright.' The diagram must distinguish rights-holder ownership from granted permissions. Do not imply all licences permit all three activities; the 'If permitted' label must appear by each branch. No actual company or licence logos; no Creative Commons badge.

Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. White background, navy headings and outlines, muted teal/blue emphasis, orange for risk. Flat illustrated textbook style, crisp large sans-serif lettering, generous whitespace, few words. Diagram relationships and pictorial meaning are more important than decoration. All requested labels must be exact, readable, and correctly spelt in British English. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'PERMISSIONS AND PRICE ARE DIFFERENT'. Main visual is a two-by-two conceptual grid with clear axis labels. LEFT vertical axis 'User permissions', top row label 'Free / open source', bottom row label 'Proprietary'. TOP horizontal axis 'Price to obtain a copy', left column label 'No charge', right column label 'Paid'. Exactly four equally sized pictorial quadrants. Top-left: open source-code document plus zero-price tag; label 'Freedoms can remain'. Top-right: same open source-code document plus money/payment icon; label 'Freedoms can remain'. Bottom-left: locked source-code document plus zero-price tag; label 'Restrictions can remain'. Bottom-right: locked source-code document plus payment icon; label 'Restrictions can remain'. Clearly readable axes outside cells, simple solid grid rules, no ambiguous arrows. Footer on two lines: 'Commercial describes business activity.' and 'It does not mean proprietary.' Do not label the horizontal axis commercial/non-commercial: zero-price distribution can also be business activity. The top row groups overlapping software-freedom concepts for this comparison, not a claim that FSF and OSI are identical organisations.

Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. White background, navy headings and outlines, muted teal/blue emphasis, orange for risk. Flat illustrated textbook style, crisp large sans-serif lettering, generous whitespace, few words. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'SHAREWARE: CHECK THE TRIAL TERMS'. A large left-to-right time diagram. Beginning a calendar labelled 'Day 1'. A teal time band from 'Day 1' to a boundary calendar labelled 'Day 30', with a laptop trial icon and caption 'Evaluate the permitted features'. From that boundary split into exactly two alternatives: upper branch ending at receipt plus working laptop labelled 'Obtain permission for continued use'; lower branch ending at closed laptop labelled 'Stop using the trial'. Small caption over the time band 'Example: a 30-day trial'. Below, separately show a source-code document and closed padlock labelled 'Source modification needs separate permission'. Footer exact: 'Trial periods and restrictions vary by offer.' Do not say all shareware expires after 30 days, that all trials are free, that paying transfers copyright, or that trial access grants source-modification rights. The main teaching content is the visible time boundary and two permitted next steps, not a table.

Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. White background, navy headings and outlines, muted teal/blue emphasis, orange for risk. Flat illustrated textbook style, crisp large sans-serif lettering, generous whitespace, few words. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'AI: FROM EVIDENCE TO ACTION'. Three large illustrated panels left to right linked by two clear forward arrows. LEFT 'Input': vibration waveform and thermometer attached to a physical factory pump, caption 'Vibration and temperature'. MIDDLE 'Inference': abstract simple pattern-recognition model comparing signal traces, caption 'Estimate a developing fault'. RIGHT 'Use of output': technician studying an alert and inspecting the same pump, caption 'Inspect and plan maintenance'. Below the main chain, two independent small caution illustrations: an alert bell beside a sound pump, labelled 'False alert: unnecessary inspection'; an unflagged pump with a worn bearing, labelled 'Missed fault: breakdown still possible'. Footer exact: 'A prediction guides a decision; it is not a guarantee.' Do not depict a humanoid robot or consciousness, do not claim the model always learns while in use, and do not draw an arrow that treats prediction as certain failure.

Create one precise educational infographic for an English-language Cambridge AS Computer Science course. Landscape 3:2. No brand logos, watermark, tiny text, invented facts, extra labels or essay paragraphs. Title: 'AVERAGE ACCURACY CAN HIDE UNEQUAL ERRORS'. At top, two side-by-side clearly separate speech inputs with two diverse adults, label 'Accent A' for the first and 'Accent B' for the second. Each arrow enters the same central box labelled 'Speech-to-text system'. From that central box split two arrows to separate lower result panels aligned with input groups. LEFT result shows transcript lines and a check icon, caption 'Mostly correct captions'. RIGHT result shows transcript lines interrupted by visibly marked question marks, caption 'Frequent caption errors'. Make group labels repeat at result panels as 'Accent A' and 'Accent B' so attribution is unambiguous. A large bracket beneath both results leads to a small average gauge labelled 'One overall score can hide the difference'. Bottom row: magnifying glass over two results and an editor pencil, with exact label 'Check each group and provide corrections'. No numerical percentages or invented counts, no stereotypes connecting appearance to competence; difference is system performance for accents. No suggestion that one accent is inherently wrong.

A split landscape illustration, with a central comparison sign, NOT a tilted scale declaring a winner. LEFT teal region title 'Potential savings': farm crops, irrigation pipes and a sensor; three short labels 'Less water extraction', 'Less unnecessary pumping', 'Better use of resources'. RIGHT muted orange region title 'System footprint': connected sensor, server, power cable, and old electronic equipment; three labels 'Computing electricity', 'Hardware manufacture', 'Replacement and waste'.
